title: Intermediate logic: metalogic, sets and incompleteness
audience: a college student in a philosophy degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Study logic about logic: naive set theory, relations, functions and cardinality (countable and uncountable sets and Cantor's diagonal argument), induction on formulas, the soundness and completeness of first-order logic, compactness and the Löwenheim-Skolem theorems, Turing machines and the halting problem, and Gödel's incompleteness theorems, using Python for set operations, encodings and diagonalization.
primary_reading: The Open Logic Project: Sets, Logic, Computation and Incompleteness and Computability (free)

weeks.4: Cantor's diagonal argument and uncountable sets
weeks.5: Induction on formulas and structural recursion
weeks.6: Soundness of propositional and first-order logic
weeks.7: Completeness: maximal consistent sets and Henkin models
weeks.9: Computability: Turing machines and the Church-Turing thesis
weeks.12: The incompleteness theorems and their philosophical significance

blocks.deliverable: Prove five set identities and check them in Python.
Build a bijection between the natural numbers and the integers.
Prove a property of all formulas by induction.
Week 7 midterm; explain the main steps of the completeness proof.
Simulate a small Turing machine in Python.
Gödel-number five formulas and decode three.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Metalogic report: write a careful proof of one major result (Cantor's theorem, the undecidability of the halting problem or the compactness theorem) with every step justified, implement a Python demonstration of its key construction (a diagonal argument, a reduction or an encoding), and write a page on the result's philosophical significance.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
